papers.title: Social media influencers can increase collective political beliefs and actions: findings from experiments and a quasi-experimental field study
papers.authors: Pascal Merz and Christian von Sikorski
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent influencer-effect mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Two experiments and a quasi-experimental field study with a real influencer examine whether influencer messages change collective political beliefs and intended action. Messages emphasizing collective response efficacy increase efficacy beliefs and action intentions, especially among followers with strong parasocial relationships. This provides a high-quality causal mechanism for how an IShowSpeed-style creator could affect followers' country-related attitudes, but it is not a China-visit study.

papers.title: Effects of travel vloggers’ attributes on tourists’ intention: the role of cynicism
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent travel-vlogger mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This study estimates a structural model linking travel-vlogger attributes, parasocial interaction, audience cynicism, and travel intention. It shows that creator characteristics work through relational responses and that cynical audiences discount persuasive cues. The paper is useful for explaining heterogeneous follower reactions to a foreign influencer's China visit, but it studies tourism persuasion generally rather than IShowSpeed or China.

papers.title: Workplace AI Usage, Intrinsic Motivation, and Job Burnout: Evidence from a Longitudinal Study
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This longitudinal study examines whether employees' workplace AI use predicts later intrinsic motivation and job burnout. Repeated observations distinguish prospective associations from same-wave correlations and test motivation as a psychological pathway connecting AI-supported work with burnout. The design directly addresses whether AI functions as a job resource or demand, although self-reported use and observational exposure limit causal inference.

papers.title: Values of China: Toward a Cultural Map
papers.category: Preprint · dissertation adjacent value measurement · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This working paper develops a synthetic-archetype method that combines narrative prompts with sentence-level embeddings to measure value and social-order themes in local Chinese folktales. County-level tale measures are related to historical geography and contemporary survey attitudes, including trust, prosocial behavior, kin obligations, effort, time orientation, and authority. It offers a measurement bridge from narrative archetypes to values, but it has not completed journal peer review.

papers.title: AI and Worker Well-being: Evidence from a Nationally Representative Study
papers.authors: Alex Bryson, Antti Kauhanen, and Petri Rouvinen
papers.category: Preprint · workplace AI and well-being · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using nationally representative Finnish cross-sectional and longitudinal data from 2018–2023, this working paper finds no systematic overall association between AI use and job satisfaction after accounting for worker and workplace characteristics. Personal involvement with AI is associated with higher engagement, while intensive use is also associated with higher burnout and replacement fears. The results show simultaneous resource and strain pathways but have not completed journal peer review.

toc.title: #BoPo, #Ideal, or #Mixed? Exploring Adolescents’ Daily Exposure to Appearance Content on Social Media and Its Relations with Body Image Components
toc.abstractEn: Daily diary evidence distinguishes exposure to idealized, body-positive, and mixed appearance content. The study tests how these content types correspond to adolescents' day-to-day body image rather than treating all appearance-related social media exposure as equivalent.

toc.title: Entertainment Contributes to Adaptive Coping: A Longitudinal Investigation of the Interplay Between Hedonic and Eudaimonic Entertainment, Escapism, and Meaning Making
toc.abstractEn: A longitudinal design examines how pleasurable and meaningful entertainment use, escapism, and meaning making develop together over time. The study takes a salutogenic perspective and tests whether entertainment can support adaptive coping beyond short-term mood effects.

toc.title: Examining the Effects of Viewing Positive Aging TikTok Videos on Aging Outcomes and Attitudes Among Young, Middle-Aged, and Older Women
toc.abstractEn: An experiment with 306 younger, 225 middle-aged, and 233 older women tests positive-aging TikTok videos using the communicative ecology model of successful aging. Outcomes include attitudes toward aging and age-related self-perceptions across life stages.

toc.title: Understanding How Immersive Media Enhance Prosociality: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis
toc.abstractEn: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence on immersive media and prosocial outcomes. It evaluates how immersion, embodiment, perspective taking, and study design relate to helping, empathy, and other prosocial responses.

toc.title: The Perfect Li(f)e: A Longitudinal Study on Positive Social Media Content and European Adolescents’ Perfectionism
toc.abstractEn: Longitudinal data from European adolescents examine whether exposure to highly positive and polished social media content predicts changes in perfectionism. The study separates content exposure from stable individual differences and traces reciprocal patterns over time.

papers.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
papers.authors: Marios Papamichalis, Laura Forastiere, and Nicholas A. Christakis
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A randomized controlled trial involving 8,331 people in 110 rural Honduran villages examines secondary network effects of a 22-month health-education intervention. Beyond its intended knowledge outcomes, the intervention changes pre-existing health, friendship, and financial ties, showing that randomized social interventions can rewire relationships among treated and untreated community members. The study is directly social-scientific and provides rare causal evidence on network spillovers.

papers.title: On sentiment recognition mechanism in Black Myth: Wukong player communication on YouTube
papers.authors: Q. Tang, X. Bai, and F. Gan
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This study analyzes 7,604 YouTube comments about Black Myth: Wukong with sentiment analysis, topic modeling, interaction thresholds, and social-network analysis. Most comments are neutral to positive, while discussions cluster around game mechanics, cultural narratives, character backgrounds, and differences between Chinese and Western interpretations. The study directly observes overseas reception of a Chinese myth-based character and narrative, although platform comments cannot by themselves identify causal effects on liking, identification, or sharing intentions.

papers.title: Audience reception of translated classic films: Zhang Yimou’s Hero in the digital English world
papers.venue: Asia Pacific Translation and Intercultural Studies, 10(3)
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using sentiment analysis and corpus-based keyword analysis of professional and general Anglophone reviews, this study examines reception of Zhang Yimou's Hero. Both groups respond positively but emphasize different aspects: complex political characters and relationships, Chinese elements and the wuxia genre, fight scenes, and aesthetic qualities. The article separates character, plot, and visual reception and attributes group differences to cultural discount, hybridity, memory, translation mode, and translation quality.
